judged_text: The placeholder assignment overwrites the parsed data's refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token", and callers persist that data — Office365's spread-merge at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 and Zoom's stored parsedToken.data — replacing the credential's real refresh token. Self-hosters who enable credential sync have the real refresh tokens of affected OAuth credentials destroyed in the database; disabling sharing or losing CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT afterwards leaves refresh_token="refresh_token", which providers reject with invalid_grant, permanently bricking those integrations until every user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, mutates the parsed result to set `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26). In Office365 refresh logic, the returned result’s `.data` is spread into the existing credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`), so the placeholder value will overwrite the real stored refresh token and then be persisted via `prisma.credential.update` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around the shown change). This is consistent with the finding’s described data-loss/bricking scenario when credential sync mode returns responses without a refresh token.
